subject.title: RFC: Readiness Providers and Hosting Profiles

question: After preserving unset-upgrade compatibility, which contract should OpenClaw accept: only the canonical readiness provider/result foundation, or also the four standard profiles and operator extensions?
rationale: The RFC creates multiple permanent public and support-policy surfaces; code review cannot determine how much of that product contract OpenClaw should own.

options.title: Accept the foundation first
options.body: Adopt the canonical result and provider registry, preserve existing unset readiness, and defer profile enforcement and operator composition to follow-up acceptance.

options.title: Accept the full stack
options.body: Adopt providers, all four standard profiles, operator extensions, and release conformance after documenting and proving the upgrade path.

options.title: Keep profiles downstream
options.body: Retain existing core readiness and let hosting integrations compose posture-specific checks without new core profile contracts.

recommendation.title: Accept the foundation first
recommendation.body: Adopt the canonical result and provider registry, preserve existing unset readiness, and defer profile enforcement and operator composition to follow-up acceptance.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent repository merger history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the cross-cutting acceptance and compatibility choice.
